newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Chronology of S.Korea's Hanbo loan scandal.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of S.Korea's Hanbo loan scandal.

text.p: A growing loans scandal on Wednesay threatened to engulf South Korean President Kim Young-sam in an election year as a cabinet minister resigned and another of Kim's trusted associates was grilled by prosecutors.
The following is a chronology of events in the loan scandal involving Hanbo Steel Corp.
Jan 23 - Leading South Korean steel maker Hanbo Steel Corp, a unit of South Korea's Hanbo Group, defaults on loan payments and creditors seek buyer for the company.
Jan 24 - Hanbo Chairman Chung Bo-Keun says Hanbo Steel will file for court receivership.
Jan 25 - South Korea's justice Ministry bans seven executives of the Hanbo Group from leaving country.
Jan 27 - President Kim Young-sam ordered investigation into Hanbo Group after the financial collapse of Hanbo Steel.
Jan 27- South Korea's ruling party bows to opposition demands and agrees to a parliamentary probe into the Hanbo Group.
Jan 27 - Hanbo Steel Co and two affiliates defaulted on debt payments totalling 131.1 billion won, officials at the Office of Bank Supervision say.
Jan 27 - A group of 61 South Korean banks and financial institutions with loans to Hanbo Steel Co say would support court receivership to keep the steel maker afloat.
Jan 28 - South Korean police raid offices of the Hanbo Group following allegations of misconduct in the loan scandal.
Jan 28 - South Korea bans heads of the four main creditor banks of Hanbo Steel from leaving the country.
Jan 29 - South Korean state prosecutors begin questioning executives of the Hanbo Group on how $5.8 billion of loans were funnelled to foundering steelmaking division.
Jan 29 - South Korean authorities open special probe into main creditors of the Hanbo Group.
Jan 30 - South Korean state prosecutors summon founder of the Hanbo Group, Chung Tae-soo, from hospital for questioning.
Jan 31 - South Korean court decides to protect debt-ridden Hanbo Steel Corp and its affiliates from creditors.
Jan 31- South Korea says it will set aside about 100 billion won ($115 million) to keep Hanbo Steel Co running and help the companies suppliers.
Jan 31 - Prosecutors arrest founder of Hanbo Group.
Feb 1 - South Korea's Pohang Iron and Steel Co Ltd (POSCO) agrees in principle to run insolvent Hanbo Steel Co
Feb 1 - South Korea pumps cash into Hanbo Steel in bid to resurrect it as central bank governor assures financial markets.
Feb 2 - President Kim calls huge loans to the conglomerate a typical example of corruption.
Feb 4 - Prosecutors question heads of two leading local banks and a former president of a state bank over loan scandal.
Feb 5 - A leading opposition member of parliament, Kwon Roh-kap, says took money from Hanbo Group founder.

Feb 5 - South Korean prosecutors arrest two leading bankers, Sheen Kwang-shik, president of Korea First Bank, and Woo Chan-mok, head of Cho Hung Bank. on charges of bribery in connection with loans extended to Hanbo Steel.
Feb 6 - Prosecutors summon two more leading bankers, Chang Myung-son, president of Korea Exchange Bank, and Kim Shi-hyung, head of state-run Korea Development Bank, for questioning.
Feb 10 - Prosecutors summon three politicians, including Hong In-gil, a close associate of President Kim Young-sam.
Feb 11 - Prosecutors arrested Hong In-gil.
Feb 12 - Home Affairs Minister Kim Woo-suk offers to resign after state prosecutors summoned him for questioning over the Hanbo loan scandal. President Kim accepts resignation.
Feb 12 - South Korean Prime Minister Lee Soo-sung said is ready to resign to take responsibility for loan scandal.
